segments.narration: America's worst fire was buried by a more famous one. Both started the same night; only one made the history books.
The eighth of October, 1871. Peshtigo, Wisconsin: a timber town in a drought, ringed by slash piles from clearing land.
A cold front raised the wind and dozens of small burns merged. Roughly 1.2 million acres went up. Between 1,500 and 2,500 people died.
Survivors described a fire tornado picking up railway cars and whole houses. The air itself was burning.
People ran for the Peshtigo River and stood in it for hours. Some drowned. Some died of cold. Chicago burned that same night.
